The test image shows a tomato stem split longitudinally, revealing extensive brown/tan discoloration of the internal vascular and cortical tissue. The plant is wilted with dead leaves visible. This is clearly a vascular disease. Top candidates: Verticillium Wilt, Bacterial Canker, or Bacterial Wilt.

I'll use my 1 reference view on Verticillium Wilt, as the internal vascular browning pattern is most characteristic of that disease.

The reference Verticillium Wilt image shows leaf-level symptoms (yellowing/wilting) on a different plant, not the internal stem browning shown in the test image.

**Analysis of the test image:**
- Tomato stem split longitudinally, lying on black plastic mulch
- Internal tissue shows pervasive brown/tan discoloration of vascular and cortical tissue
- Plant has completely collapsed with dead wilted leaves scattered around
- Some whitish/lighter tissue visible at the pith center

This presentation (split stem showing vascular browning + whole plant death) is classic for a vascular wilt disease. Verticillium Wilt characteristically shows brown vascular streaking in the stem when cut — this is a standard diagnostic technique for the disease. The pattern of brown cortex/vascular tissue throughout the stem length is highly consistent with Verticillium Wilt in tomato.
